_comment: H2 profile -> serving-params map. PROJECTED defaults encoding the 12-config hardware matrix (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-11-agent-capabilities-and-hardware-matrix.md). install.ps1 Step 6 reads the profile id + ram_tier emitted by detect.ps1 and renders the backend llama-swap template with these values. H3 (selftest.ps1) MEASURES on each real box and refines these numbers; nothing here is measured yet.

_fields.cache_ram_mib_by_ram_tier: TOP-LEVEL (not per tier): llama-server host-RAM prompt cache (--cache-ram, MiB) rendered into every llama.cpp seat by RAM tier. The server parks evicted slots' KV in RAM and restores them on a prefix match (agent-loop steps, re-delegated docs). llama-server default is 8192 on every build; these values replace it per box. The FLOOR RULE (2026-09-21): llama-server's own default is 8192 MiB on every build, so this map may only hand a box LESS than that where its RAM genuinely cannot carry it (min = a 4 GB laptop), and otherwise hands the bigger boxes what they actually have. The first cut broke that rule in the losing direction — 2048 on the 32 GB nodes and 6144 on the 64 GB one, i.e. a silent cut below the default they had been running on. Values are still unmeasured against a contract stream; Task 3a of plans/2026-09-20-llamacpp-prompt-cache-tiers.md sets them from measurement. A full 32k slot costs ~1.1 GB, so these hold roughly 1 / 7 / 15 / 22 of them. vLLM seats keep LMCache and never get this flag.
_fields.alt_backends: optional: extra serving backends this tier renders BESIDE its primary one on the same box (the renderer knows one family, ["cpu"]: the tier's chat weights as <id>-cpu entries run by a CPU llama-server build, joined to the interactive set; rendered only when `install render --llama-bin-cpu <dir>` is given). NO tier declares it: amd-gcn's ["cpu"] was withdrawn 2026-09-24 by operator order, because no model may run on CPU (ADR 0054 amendment). Declared per tier and MEASURED before it ships.
_fields.long_ctx_size: optional: the LONG window a tier serves on a dedicated opt-in twin seat (the `-262k` entry the template renders with a literal --ctx-size), for tiers whose extra cards buy context. 0/absent = no long twin. The composite tier routes window overflow to it.
_fields.kv_type: q8_0|f16 -> --cache-type-k/--cache-type-v (kept symmetric; q8_0 V requires flash-attn on).
_fields.agent_ctx_tokens: value for the agent's -ctx-tokens (compaction budget); matches ctx_size.
_fields.resident_tier: the workhorse seat (gemma4-26b-a4b|offload-e4b|gemma4-e2b) — ttl 300 like every entry; resident is a ROLE in the matrix set, never permanence. SEEDS the agent planner seat: install seed derives config agent_model from it when it differs from the workhorse (internal/tierseed); override or blank via config_seed.agent_model.
_fields.include_26b: whether the 26B-A4B model appears in the rendered yaml + swap group at all.
_fields.include_qwen38: whether the Qwen3.8-27B coder/agent model renders into the serving yaml (entry + resident-set membership where the template is all-resident) and its GGUF+mmproj join the install download set. Mirrors the include_26b mechanism.
_fields.include_qwen35_4b: whether the Qwen3.5-4B AGENT seat renders into the serving yaml (entry + swappable-set membership) and its GGUF joins the install download set. Mirrors the include_qwen38 mechanism. This is the small-tier counterpart: a 3.5GB agent seat for tiers whose workhorse is too weak to plan well but which cannot afford a 27B.
_fields.include_qwen35_9b: whether the Qwen3.5-9B AGENT seat renders into the serving yaml (entry + swappable-set membership) and its GGUF joins the install download set. Mirrors the include_qwen35_4b mechanism, one weight class up: a 5.6GB agent seat for the 8GB tiers (6344 MiB at 16K / 6696 MiB at 32K, measured on the blackwell-8 reference box 2026-08-22). MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with include_qwen35_4b - both entries claim the agent-seat alias, and the renderer refuses a tier that sets both.
_fields.include_mimo_9b: whether the mimo-9b-agent seat (XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B, bartowski GGUF Q4_K_M) renders into the serving yaml (entry + swappable-set membership) and its GGUF joins the install download set. A SECOND 8GB-class agent seat measured 2026-09-24 a coin-flip quality tie against include_qwen35_9b (18/18 shape B x6 both 8GB reference boxes; shape C 5/5 vs 4/5, splitting by box) with a smaller VRAM footprint at the same 65536 window. It claims the SAME agent-seat alias as include_qwen35_4b and include_qwen35_9b, but pairing it with EITHER is no longer a render refusal (2026-09-24, the amd-gcn onboarding, superseding the 4B refusal shipped with this seat's own introduction): the smaller entry stays rendered as the tier's un-aliased ROLLBACK seat (the renderer moves the shared agent-seat alias to mimo-9b-agent via that entry's own __Q354B_AGENT_ALIAS__/__Q359B_AGENT_ALIAS__ token). REQUIRES llama.cpp >= b11102 (upstream llama.cpp #29319 - an older build misroutes MiMo's compact tool-call XML to the Qwen3-Coder parser and every tool call runs to the token cap). On a Vulkan UMA tier (amd-gcn) the rendered entry serves the TIER's own window/KV/flash-attn (__CTX__/__KV_K__/__KV_V__/__FLASH_ATTN__), not the literal 65536/q8_0 pin the CUDA 8GB tiers measured on their fixed-VRAM cards — see llama-swap.linux-vulkan.yaml.
_fields.moe_26b: gpu (-ngl 99, experts on GPU) | cpu_moe (--cpu-moe, experts in RAM) | drop (omit 26B). When cpu_moe, install.ps1 drops the 26B if ram_tier is low/min (no RAM path).
_fields.n_cpu_moe: optional, with moe_26b n_cpu_moe: the N of `--n-cpu-moe N`, the top N expert layers of the 26B placed in host RAM (the rest on the GPU). Refused at render when it names no N (that renders the every-expert `--cpu-moe`) or when it exceeds n_cpu_moe_max.
_fields.n_cpu_moe_max: optional: the tier's MEASURED spill (INV-1, register H-01): the most expert layers a measurement showed may be placed in host RAM. A separate number from n_cpu_moe on purpose - the placement a tier ships and the ceiling its measurement supports are two decisions, and one field cannot check itself. `install render` refuses a config whose `--n-cpu-moe` exceeds it; 0 or absent means the tier recorded no measured spill, so none is sanctioned. No shipped tier declares one.
_fields.backend: the llama-swap.<os>-<backend> template this profile renders from (cuda|vulkan|cpu|dual-cuda; rk3588 is the Rockchip RK3588 SoC, Linux only: llama.cpp on Vulkan for the tier's GPU entry plus rkllm NPU seats, from a template that lists only models that fit its shared-RAM budget).
_fields.dual_resident: dual-gpu only: render two models resident (no shared exclusive swap group).
_fields.gpu_env: env vars added to EVERY model in the rendered serving config, appended after whatever the template already declares. Was an `if ($profileId -match '^blackwell-')` branch inside install.ps1, so a Linux install of the same tier silently did not get it. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES pins the device (hybrid-graphics can resolve the default to -1); CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY is llama.cpp #22696.
_fields.media_seats: ALIAS-backed media capabilities this tier serves, rendered into BOTH the llama-swap models map and the harness config binding that routes to them (internal/mediaseat). Each seat: kind (vision|stt|ocr|rkllm), name (the llama-swap model id AND the binding value), aliases, model/mmproj/vad_model (relative to the models dir), bin + lib_dir for a seat that is not llama-server (may carry __OFFLOAD_HOME__/__EXE__), ctx_size (vision runs its own smaller window), residency (swappable|resident - a ROLE, since group names are per-template), ttl, and extra (true = a registered extra: rendered into llama-swap and reachable by name and aliases, but bound to NO config key and not counted by the one-writer check, so a tier can serve a second vision/ocr/stt model beside the bound one; not on rkllm, no tasks). An rkllm seat is an NPU LLM/VLM served by the Rockchip RKLLM runtime, not llama-server: it takes model (a .rkllm), an optional vision_encoder (a .rknn under the models dir; with one the seat is a VLM and writes vision_model, without one it is a chat model and writes nothing), ctx_size and cpu_mask (hex, default 0x0f = the A55 cluster; at least 3 bits, the runtime refuses fewer than the SoC has NPU cores), and bin defaults to the launcher the rknpu accelerator ships. A tier declaring NO seat leaves vision_model/stt_model empty and the route honestly defers. FILE-backed media (image/video/music) is NOT here - those are spawn-per-job subprocesses under the GPU lease, seeded via config_seed and derived by internal/mediacap.
_fields.vllm_seat: optional: the tier's persistent vLLM AGENT-LANE seat (ADR 0035, 0048, 0049) - one declaration renders the llama-swap entry, the start/stop wrappers and unit, and the harness config bindings (agent_model, vllm_seats, the kv_cache_server binding). It renders only when the box has the hand-built venv and the weights, else the tier falls back to fallback_agent_model with the reason printed. storeless_reason is the MEASURED reason the seat has no cache server; it is carried verbatim into its kv_cache_server binding and is refused beside a cache_server.
_fields.extra_vllm_seats: optional, needs vllm_seat: the tier's further vLLM seats (ADR 0048 Amendment 2). KEYS ARE STRICT: a key that is not a vllm_seat field is refused by tier and JSON path at parse, never silently dropped (a misspelt storeless_reason would otherwise seed the generic reason). on-demand seats served beside the lane seat on the SAME card, never the agent lane (agent_model, the fallback and every bound-lane field are refused on one). Each is validated like the lane seat minus the fallback, must share its card, and must not repeat any id, alias or unit. Each renders only when the box has the venv, ITS weights and the wrapper scripts its entry runs; an active one joins the box's vllm_seats roster with its own kv_cache_server binding, and the layer that names it (by id or alias) is seeded only while it is - a layer whose vLLM seat is absent is dropped, and a layer set that loses `single` seeds none. The renderer emits every vLLM seat of a tier as an ALTERNATIVE of the others in the residents set (two seats at util 0.90 cannot share a card). A layer seat naming a vLLM seat must equal its max_model_len as ctx_tokens (and its max_num_seqs as max_inflight, when set). The installer renders the seat's llama-swap entry; its systemd unit, its wrapper scripts (named after the unit: <unit>-run.sh, <unit>-cmd.sh, <unit>-cmdstop.sh) and its polkit rule are the operator's, which is also why the two wrapper scripts (<unit>-cmd.sh, <unit>-cmdstop.sh) are its prerequisite: a box advertises the seat only once they are in the seat directory.
_fields.composes: COMPOSITE TIERS (ADR 0052, 0.116.0): the tier ids this tier is a COMPLETE instance of at the same time (blackwell-3x16 composes blackwell-16 and blackwell-2x16). Every id must be a tier in this table, none may be composite itself, and a tier never composes itself. Seeded into config as tiers = composes + this id and tier_profile = this id (internal/tierseed.Resolve); health and offload_status advertise them. Requires layers - composes without layers seeds nothing and is refused at parse.
_fields.layers: COMPOSITE TIERS: the device layers this box places work onto, seeded VERBATIM into config.layers and validated at parse (Doc.Validate) and at resolve (config.ValidateLayers). KEYS ARE STRICT: every layers[] / layers[].seats[] key must be one documented below, spelled exactly - a key the decoder cannot match is refused by tier and JSON path at parse (tierseed.ParseDoc, so the installer's embedded copy too) and at config load (config.ValidateLayerKeys), never dropped to a 0 that turns a fail-closed guard fail-open. A box whose config carries no layers has one implicit layer and is byte-identical on every result, health, status and ledger surface. ONE placement rule (internal/placement.Decide) reads these at runtime on the box, on the delegator for a remote node's advertised layers, and again at admission on the node.
_fields.layers[].name: the layer id placement records and a contract may request (`layer` on the wire): single | pair | triple | display | fast (the ampere-16 fast digest layer). Unique per box, ^[a-z0-9_-]{1,32}$.
_fields.layers[].tier: the composed tier this layer stands for (blackwell-16 for single, blackwell-2x16 for pair). Must be in composes or be this tier.
_fields.layers[].devices: the device SETS this layer may occupy, documentary ("0", "2" | "0,2" | "0,1,2" | "1"). Seats carry the actual pin; placed.devices on a result is the SEAT's pin, never this list.
_fields.layers[].seats: the roles served on this layer, at most one per role. The pair layer's agent seat may be left BARE ({"role": "agent"}): Resolve fills model/device/ctx_tokens/max_inflight from vllm_seat (first alias, device, max_model_len, max_num_seqs) when the box runs the vLLM seat, else from fallback_agent_model/fallback_agent_ctx_tokens on the seat's device, so one number lives in one place.
_fields.layers[].opt_in: a layer that is never the default for any task class: the triple layer is entered on an explicit context_class long only, never on load.
_fields.layers[].dormant: declared but never placed until the operator flips it to false after reading the measurement (the display layer, council R7). One config edit, operator-only.
_fields.layers[].display_device: the device the display guards read live: a CUDA index in this table; the live box pins it by GPU-UUID because the board reorders indices on power loss.
_fields.layers[].display_floor_gib: the VRAM the desktop keeps on display_device. The display_floor guard admits a seat only while free(display_device) - seat.display_footprint_gib >= this (a free-VRAM-only check admitted a 10.5 GB load onto a card with 9 GB free; council R6). >= 4 GiB on the 3-card box: the 2026-09-04 starvation dropped the desktop to 720p and forced a reboot.
_fields.layers[].guards: the live checks an admission on this layer must pass, from display_floor | presence | host_ram. Every guard fails CLOSED: a probe that cannot read refuses, and operator_presence defaults to present.
_fields.layers[].seats[].role: router | agent | long | ocr | vision | stt - the closed vocabulary the placement table keys on. router carries no model (its rungs come from model_map / the cascade); every other role needs one.
_fields.layers[].seats[].model: the llama-swap id or alias served for this role on this layer. It must be a seat the composite serving template renders (D5 checked union).
_fields.layers[].seats[].device: this seat's CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES pin under CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID: "0" | "2" | "0,2" | "0,1,2" | "1". Required on every seat. Device 1 is the display card on the 3-card box: only the triple and display layers may name it.
_fields.layers[].seats[].ctx_tokens: the seat's SERVED window, read from config and never probed before admission. Sizes the contract context cap (min(2 MiB, largest window x 3)) and the window-overflow decision.
_fields.layers[].seats[].max_inflight: vLLM max_num_seqs for the seat; 0 = never saturated by count (llama.cpp seats). A saturated pair is RECORDED in placed.reason, never acted on (council R2).
_fields.layers[].seats[].footprint_gib: VRAM this seat puts on EACH device of its pin, measured alone (26B 13,301 MiB; vl-8b 11,751; whisper ~2,182; 27b-262k 14.3+15.5 GB; flash-next-262k 13.0/10.5/12.5 GB; the vLLM pair seat ~15 GiB per card at util 0.90). Used to name the eviction a placement would cause on a shared device set.
_fields.layers[].seats[].display_footprint_gib: VRAM this seat puts on the layer's display_device. REQUIRED (> 0) on a display_floor-guarded layer for every seat whose pin includes the display device - a 0 degrades the guard to the rejected free-VRAM check, and config refuses it at load.
_fields.layers[].seats[].host_ram_gib: host RAM the seat holds while loaded (experts on CPU: flash-next-262k ~70 GB). The host_ram guard refuses when free host RAM is below it. REQUIRED (> 0) on every seat of a host_ram-guarded layer - the guard is free >= this, and a 0 admits the load on every box; config refuses the omission at load and the table at parse.
_fields.layers[].seats[].prefill_tps: measured prompt-processing rate. The long seats are entered only when tokens / this <= the contract's budget: flash-next-262k prefills at 69 t/s, so a 200k prompt is ~48 min against a 900 s cap; the pair's 27b-262k at 1,197 t/s takes window overflow instead. REQUIRED (> 0) on every long seat - a 0 rate is a division by zero on the first long placement; config refuses the omission at load and the table at parse.
_fields.layers[].seats[].model_map: router role only: route key (workhorse | triage) -> the twin model served on THIS layer, so the dormant display layer can substitute its device-1 twins for the cascade's rungs.

_accelerator_fields.kind: npu | tpu — the device class (hailo-8l and rknpu are npus, coral-edgetpu a tpu). An accelerator is ADDITIVE to a box's GPU tier (ADR 0024): `profile` stays one string and `accelerators` lists what rides beside it.
_accelerator_fields.owns: the offload_* capabilities this accelerator serves EXCLUSIVELY when present; the GPU tier keeps everything else (VQA/description stay on the VLM; OCR stays GPU-primary with engine:npu as the caller's explicit fast path).
_accelerator_fields.config_seed: config.json keys merged AFTER the GPU tier's seed (internal/tierseed.ResolveAccelerators). Each device has its own home token: __HAILO_HOME__ expands to the Hailo repo checkout (installer env HAILO_HOME, default <OFFLOAD_HOME>/hailo), __CORAL_HOME__ to the Coral sidecar home (CORAL_HOME, default <OFFLOAD_HOME>/coral), __RKNPU_HOME__ to the RKNPU sidecar home (RKNPU_HOME, default <OFFLOAD_HOME>/rknpu).
_accelerator_fields.detect: how detect.ps1 / hwdetect recognise the device — documentation of the rule implemented in code.

hailo-8l.detect: hailortcli scan lists a device AND hailortcli fw-control identify reports 'Device Architecture: HAILO8L'
hailo-8l.notes: Hailo-8L M.2 (HM21LB1C2KAE), HailoRT 4.24.0 + model zoo v2.19.0 hailo8l HEFs — the current matched pair (5.x is the Hailo-10/15 line). Sidecar = harness-spawned on demand over loopback HTTP, self-exits idle (operator decision 2026-08-22: no scheduler, clean box). Measured on <node-e>: ArcFace same-person 0.853 vs different ≤0.106; YOLOv8s on-chip NMS; TinyCLIP-61M 512-d. Windows cannot see the device as an NPU (no MCDM driver) — irrelevant to this route. The sidecar launcher is __HAILO_HOME__/hailo-http.cmd and HAILO_HOME defaults to <OFFLOAD_HOME>/hailo, so an install whose sidecar checkout lives elsewhere sets HAILO_HOME before the installer runs; an existing config.json is never re-pointed.

coral-edgetpu.detect: /sys/class/apex/apex_0/status reads ALIVE (gasket/apex driver bound; Linux only — Windows has no apex driver and never matches)
coral-edgetpu.notes: Coral Edge TPU (M.2 A+E on <node-c>, PCI 03:00.0; one id for the whole family — USB/M.2/Dual all run the same _edgetpu.tflite artifacts). Runtime as measured 2026-09-04 (Ecosystem/<node-c>/2026-09-04_coral-tpu/SETUP.md): feranick gasket-dkms 1.0-18.4 + libedgetpu1-std 16.0TF2.19.1 + ai-edge-litert 2.2.0 (cp314); MobileNet v2 iNat p50 3.16 ms / ~300 inf/s, 70-71 C sustained, no throttle; -max measured indistinguishable (the ~3 ms floor is the Gen2 x1 transfer, not compute) and purged. The tier READS that configuration and never rewrites it: the sidecar (accelerators/coral/server.py, harness-spawned on demand over loopback, self-exits idle) reads sysfs temp/status only. Four capabilities in v1, every model from google-coral/test_data (Apache-2.0) and verified by sha256 in accelerators/coral/models.json: classify_image (EfficientNet-EdgeTPU-S ImageNet; MobileNet v2 iNat birds/insects/plants), object_detect (EfficientDet-Lite0/1/2 COCO), semantic_segment (DeepLabV3 MNv2 Pascal, 21 classes — semantic, NOT the Hailo's instance `segment`), image_embed (EfficientNet-EdgeTPU-S extractor, 1280-d, space efficientnet-edgetpu-s — not CLIP, so no text tower and no zero_shot). Shared-name rule (D5): object_detect and image_embed are capability names one owner per box — the FIRST listed accelerator that owns a name registers it. Deploy on <node-c> (D8): CORAL_HOME=<OFFLOAD_HOME>/coral with its own venv from the staged cp314 wheels; the fleet unit's ProtectHome=yes hides ~/coral-venv, which stays the operator's bench.

rknpu.detect: one of the sysfs uevent files below carries the whole line DRIVER=RKNPU (Rockchip's NPU driver bound). Vendor 6.1 BSP kernel: /sys/class/drm/card0..card3/device/uevent (the NPU is the DRM card's own device). Mainline kernel with the out-of-tree rknpu (DKMS) driver: the DRM card's device is virtual and its uevent EMPTY, so the line is read from /sys/bus/platform/devices/fdab0000.npu, fdac0000.npu and fdad0000.npu/uevent (the three cores; any one bound is enough). The mainline in-tree driver binds the same cores as DRIVER=rocket and is deliberately NOT matched: the RKNN runtime does not run on it. Linux only — Windows has no sysfs and never matches
rknpu.notes: Rockchip RK3588 / RK3588S NPU (6 TOPS, 3 cores). Driver: the vendor rknpu, built into the 6.1 BSP kernel or, on a mainline kernel, the out-of-tree DKMS build (0.9.8) with the in-tree `rocket` driver blacklisted — rocket is a different driver that the RKNN runtime does not use. Measured on <node-d> (RK3588S: 4x A55 + 4x A76, 7.7 GiB shared LPDDR4X): librknnrt 2.3.2 ran resnet18_for_rk3588.rknn (the Rockchip prebuilt the sidecar served until 2026-09-30; core mask 0_1_2) at 2.94 ms/inference (340 FPS) on the vendor kernel's driver 0.9.7 and at 3.58 ms (279.5 FPS) on the mainline 7.0 kernel with the DKMS driver 0.9.8. The models the sidecar serves now — PP-YOLOE+ s int8 (object_detect), ResNet-50 with torchvision IMAGENET1K_V2 weights (classify_image) and CLIP ViT-B/32 (image_embed), none under an AGPL or GPL licence — were converted and checked on the toolkit's simulator on 2026-09-30 and have not run on the NPU yet, so their latency is unmeasured. An .rknn is compiled for one target SoC (rk3588). The sidecar (accelerators/rknpu/server.py) speaks the Coral's contract — harness-spawned on demand over loopback, self-exits idle, models verified by sha256 — and serves three capabilities in v1: classify_image (ImageNet), object_detect (COCO), image_embed (a CLIP-class image tower; the result names its `space`, which is not the Hailo's TinyCLIP or the Coral's EfficientNet at any dimension). All three names are shared with the Hailo and/or the Coral, so the shared-name rule (ADR 0037) gives each to the FIRST listed owner. No text tower is served: no text_embed / zero_shot, and OCR / STT engine:npu stay Hailo-only. The NPU shares system memory with the host, so a resident model holds RAM until rknpu_idle_sec passes. The service user must be able to open the NPU's DRM node under /dev/dri (root, or a member of the node's group: render on the reference board). Linux only.

blackwell-16.notes: Config #1 (5060 Ti 16GB, Blackwell sm_120). 26B resident full-GPU (-ngl 99). REQUIRES the Blackwell CUDA-12.8 sm_120 build (Task H4) - the pinned 12.4 asset lacks sm_120 and the 13.x asset segfaults the MMQ kernel into a ~5.6x-slower cuBLAS fallback. H3 may push ctx to 64K with q8. config_seed: quality-first media bindings attributed to this exact tier [see the MEASURED-STATUS CLARIFICATION at the end of this note — this string simultaneously claimed PROVEN, PROJECTED, and 'informed by a LIVE REFERENCE, not a runtime measurement' about the same seat] (bf16 O1 = 3.9min/2048 render via RAM offload; needs the model downloads + >=~48GB system RAM — see SETUP-AGENT). TIER DURABILITY (2026-08-14, operator rule): the pooled 2x16 tier moved its image seat to Krea 2 Turbo (24.5GB — physically does not fit one 16GB card); HiDream-O1 bf16 via RAM offload REMAINS this tier's measured, quality-first binding. A 32GB-tier seat change is never an argument to change a 16GB-tier seed; this tier evolves only on measurements taken at 16GB. PROJECTED. J-media 2026-07-28: media_seats are informed by a LIVE REFERENCE, not a runtime measurement. This tier IS the workstation, and its hand-built llama-swap serves the same qwen3-vl-8b (Q8_0 weights + FULL-PRECISION F16 mmproj, ctx 16384) plus whisper large-v3-turbo. The Q8 + F16-tower pairing is the 8->16GB unlock: Q4 is where small-screenshot-text fidelity died, and this one seat owns screenshots/GUI/document OCR, which is why no separate OCR model exists (hence the 'ocr' alias here and on the other tiers that inherit this seat). DELTAS FROM LIVE, deliberate and NOT measured: the seat inherits this tier's q8_0 KV while the live entry sets no cache-type at all and therefore runs F16; and it adds --image-max-tokens 2048 + --no-context-shift, neither of which live carries. Same weights and window, tighter KV, an explicit image bound. Swappable, so the ~10GB seat is the only heavy seat loaded. (The former qwen3-asr HQ STT tier was RETIRED 2026-08-14 — Seat Frontier Leg 2 consolidated STT to the whisper seat after a paired house A/B tied on quality; stt_model_hq stays empty, hq falls back to stt_model by design.) TIER-DOCTRINE PASS 2026-08-16: agent seat pointed at the VALIDATED thinking-on 26B agent entry (0/15->12/15 at D1 with reasoning on, 2026-08-10) instead of the derived reasoning-off cascade seat (measured 0% as agent). Same weights as the 26B — no new download. Capability parity with the twin-arch sibling(s) is field-identical by design; the arch split (sm86/sm120/sm70) is a BUILD concern only. MEASURED-STATUS CLARIFICATION 2026-09-07: this note previously asserted PROVEN, PROJECTED and 'informed by a LIVE REFERENCE, not a runtime measurement' about the same seat — three incompatible claims in one string, which is exactly why a notes field must never be read as a measurement status. WHAT IS TRUE: this tier HAD a real reference box. The workstation (<node-b>) ran as blackwell-16 on a SINGLE RTX 5060 Ti 16GB (sm_120, 16310 MiB, PCIe Gen3 x8 electrical) + i9-10980XE + 128GB DDR4-3400 from 2026-07-12 to 2026-08-02; the classifier self-identified blackwell-16 on it 2026-07-27; and a capability report from that box is committed at docs/tiers/reports/blackwell-16-node-b.md (banner: HISTORICAL). Evidence: Benchmarks and Optimizations/2026-08-31-48gb-gates-NOTES.md, 2026-09-01-vllm-lmcache-results/, 2026-09-03-seat-optimization-program.md, 2026-09-05-cudax/. TWO DEVICE ORDERINGS ARE IN PLAY AND THE DISPLAY CARD HAS A DIFFERENT INDEX IN EACH -- gpu_env is CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES under CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID (display = 1), while the ComfyUI pool keys are 'cuda:N' in ComfyUI's FASTEST-FIRST order (display = cuda:0, the pair = cuda:1/cuda:2). Applied, matching what the reference box actually runs (verified in both live config files and the live llama-swap header): vision seat CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES 1 -> 2 and STT 0 -> 2, the 2026-08-31 G1 singles rebalance that moved whisper, vl-8b/ocr and the embed/rerank alternates to 5060Ti#2 while the cascade + memory-stack residents stayed on card 0 (re-measured 2026-09-05: vl-8b 11,751 MiB on card 2); imagegen_pool_compute cuda:0 -> cuda:1 with donor cuda:2, the pair, bf16 and re-verified there after the 2026-09-01 revert with two 1568x880 Krea 2 Turbo stills. VIDEOGEN COMPUTE IS UNCHANGED AND MUST STAY cuda:0: an int8 DiT cannot compute on a non-default CUDA device (ComfyUI-MultiGPU #220) and the 2026-09-01 attempt to move it threw cudaErrorIllegalAddress mid-render, so its compute genuinely belongs on the display card as a documented law exception. Do not 'restore' the vision seat to device 1: at 11,751 MiB it would leave ~3.5 GiB after the ~0.5-1.5 GB DWM tax, under the >=4 GiB desktop floor set by the 2026-09-04 starvation (720p-class mode, reboot, clean event log). Operator decision 2026-09-07: the 5070 Ti is CONTEXT/KV ONLY -- it may grow the KV pool for long-context seats (137,898 tokens across three cards vs 78,506 across two) and the named opt-in over-2-card seats may span it, but no tier seat is pinned to it. VISION SEAT UPGRADED 2026-09-08 (0.113.35): qwen3-vl-8b -> qwen3-vl-32b for VISION, with the 8B KEEPING OCR. This is a quality binding and the tier was shipping the loser of its own bake-off. 48 GB gates on the reference box: visioncanary MMMU 0.740 vs the 8B's 0.630 (+11 points, clears the >=8 promotion bar) -> the 32B takes vision; DocVQA ANLS 0.928 (-3.7) plus a dense-transcription regression -> the 8B keeps OCR. The split is itself quality-driven: each role goes to the model that measured better AT THAT ROLE, which is why this must not be collapsed back to one seat. The decision was APPLIED on the box (both live config files bind vision_model=qwen3-vl-32b and ocr_model=qwen3-vl-8b, and the running llama-swap serves both) and the tier table was simply never updated, so every fresh install of the tier whose reference box IS that machine got a measured 11-point MMMU regression. Flags are the measured ones: -sm tensor --tensor-split 25,25 on the 5060 Ti pair (CUDA-X 2026-09-05 moved it from -sm layer at the same split and got BYTE-IDENTICAL output 5/5 on a fixed image+prompt while generation went 19.6 -> 34.1 t/s -- identical output is what makes it free rather than a trade), --image-min-tokens 1024 as the visual-token FLOOR, and Qwen3-VL's official sampler (temp 0.7 / top-p 0.8 / top-k 20) pinned as a set. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,2 -- a 32B does not fit one 16 GB card and device 1 is the display card. NOT PROPAGATED TO blackwell-2x16: this seat spans BOTH cards of its pair, and on the 2-card tier the second card is the one paying the desktop/DWM tax, so a 2-card box would be asked to give ~25 GB of its 32 GB to a swappable vision seat. That tier needs its own fit measurement before it inherits this. Gated by TestTripleBlackwellVisionSeatIsTheMeasuredWinner. MEDIA ROSTER AUDITED AND GATED 2026-09-14 (0.118.1, A-15): the 48 GB bake-off (`2026-08-31-48gb-bakeoff-renders/`) ran the whole media lane on this box and the tier shipped a media block copied byte-for-byte from blackwell-2x16; PR #264 corrected the PLACEMENTS and #266 the vision MODEL, but nothing gated what the bake-off DECIDED about models and precision, so the roster could drift back into a copy without failing anything. Slot by slot: vision = qwen3-vl-32b on the pair (MMMU +11); ocr = qwen3-vl-8b on card 2 (the 32B regressed: DocVQA -3.7 plus dense transcription); stt = whisper large-v3-TURBO on card 2 (turbo wins or ties every group, es-long WER 0.0652 vs 0.0838, at ~2x the speed, so the proposed stt_hq lane FAILED and stays empty); imagegen = Krea 2 TURBO bf16 at 8 steps / cfg 1 on pool cuda:1 + donor cuda:2 (Turbo bf16 came back pristine on all four prompts, while Krea 2 RAW is BROKEN on ComfyUI 0.34.0 under every recipe tested - int8 and bf16, euler+er_sde over simple/normal, raw_dynamic shift, AuraFlow 3.1 - composition correct and buried in terminal noise where the same-seed Turbo render is clean, so RAW is a fine-tuning base and not a servable lane); videogen = LTX-2.5 int8-convrot with the CONV video VAE on compute cuda:0 + donor cuda:2 (round 2 of the decoder A/B held seed, prompt, sampler, resolution and placement constant and changed only the VAE: conv resolved more detail on every one of 5 pairs, +15-25% Laplacian energy and +9-11% high-frequency, start-frame fidelity a wash at 0.02-0.26 dB, AND conv was 12-15% faster - it wins on both measurable axes; cuda:0 remains the documented ComfyUI-MultiGPU #220 exception, not a preference). ONE SLOT HAS NO WINNER AND WAS LEFT ALONE: TTS. Chatterbox v3 and both Spanish packs transcribe back verbatim through the whisper seat (intelligibility proven, loudness -16..-18 LUFS, the es-es pack peaking +0.2 dBFS), but naturalness was explicitly left as an operator A/B and adoption needs a contained-venv bump, so the seed is unchanged and the gate says nothing about it. Gated by TestTripleBlackwellMediaRosterIsTheMeasuredOne. FAN-OUT TWIN WIRED 2026-09-14 (0.118.1, A-70): the llama.cpp 27B seat shipped `--parallel 1` and is FLAT under fan-out - 34.6-37.4 tok/s aggregate at c1..c32, and it answers 429 from c16 (6 of 16 and 22 of 32 requests failed in the baseline arm). The measured operating point on the SAME pair is `--parallel 8` at the SAME `-c` (arm par8-pair, 2026-09-01, `llamacpp-par8-pair.json`, ledger "FAIRNESS ARM par8-pair"): W1 43.4 tok/s (unchanged single-stream) and aggregate 78.7 / 110.8 / 100.7 / 106.8 at c4/8/16/32, 0 failures - about 3x aggregate under fan-out. IT SHIPS AS A SEPARATE ENTRY, `qwen3.8-27b-par8`, NOT as a flag on the seat, and that is the whole decision: llama.cpp divides `-c` among its slots, so eight slots at --ctx-size 131072 serve 16,384 tokens EACH. The same night's <node-c> arm proves the mechanism in-house (`--parallel 8 -c 32768`: "16k/32k prompts exceed the 4k/slot window"). Putting `--parallel 8` on the seat itself would therefore cut this tier's declared fallback agent lane (fallback_agent_model qwen3.8-27b, fallback_agent_ctx_tokens 131072) to 16,384 while the profile still advertised 131,072 - the advertise-more-than-you-serve defect that shipped once already on blackwell-8. Both entries are swappable alternatives at ttl 300, so the twin costs nothing until something asks for it. NOT --parallel 16: on this pair it FAILS TO START at `-c 131072` (5.0 GB recurrent-state cache) and at `-c 65536`, and needs `-c 49152` + `--tensor-split 27,23` to run at all, for 119 vs 111 at c16. NOT --parallel 32: infeasible, ~350 MB of GDN recurrent state PER SLOT (an 11.3 GB rs buffer beside ~9 GB of weights on a 16 GB card). Gated by TestPairSpanningTemplatesShipTheMeasuredFanoutTwin. The three-card arm is not what ships: par8-3c (tensor-split 17,16,17, `-c 65536`) reached 102.9 tok/s at c8 against the pair's 110.8 AND it spans the display card, which the placement law forbids - so the twin is pair-pinned (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,2) like every other default seat here. COMPOSITE (0.116.0, ADR 0052): composes blackwell-16 and blackwell-2x16 as layers single (cards 0|2) and pair (0,2), plus a DORMANT display layer for the small cascade rungs (the operator flips dormant:false after reading the G1b measurement); placement is recorded on every result as placed; the pair's long seat qwen3.8-27b-262k takes window overflow (pp 1,197 t/s) only when the pair's agent seat is idle. No TRIPLE layer is declared: the 3-card pipeline seat belongs to opencode (AGENT SEAT above), so the pair's agent seat is the home agent seat (placement.AgentHome) and no contract can name a three-card layer. The RAM-is-overflow-only rule of 2026-09-10 still removed the Flash-Next arms (0.115.4), and context_class long still resolves to the pair's 262k twin.
TWO MEDIA CALLS AT ONCE NEEDS THE PIN CLEARED (GPU routing P13b, 2026-10-03). The seed pins every single-card ComfyUI route with comfy_cuda_device "2", and on a host that leases cards an explicit pin is a hard constraint: a call that names ComfyUI device 2 queues for that card, FIFO, however many others are free. With gpu_comfy_order NOT declared the pin cannot be turned into a card, so every single-card call keeps the whole-node lease and today's --cuda-device 2 (safe, and the complaint is not fixed); with the order declared (each card's fastest-first ComfyUI position as an nvidia-smi index, "1,0,2" on this box, measured with a CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<uuid> probe) the pinned calls run on card 2 and serialise there while cards 0 and 1 stay free for text seats. Two concurrent renders on two cards need comfy_cuda_device cleared in the host's live config: the allocator then picks a free non-display card and never the display card while the operator is at the desk. The seed is left alone on purpose: on a host that does not lease cards the pin is the only thing keeping renders off the display card (TestTripleBlackwellNeverSchedulesOntoTheDisplayCard). The per-card instances use ports 8189 to 8191 (8189 plus the card's nvidia-smi index); reserve them in the host's port record.

vllm_seat.measured: The ampere-16 reference box (NVIDIA A2 16 GB, 40 W / 1200 MHz lock), vLLM 0.29.0 + the checkpoint's embedding patch, 2026-09-16. Qwen3.8-27B 3-bit GSQ (ISTA-DASLab; transformer 3-bit g128, embedding+LM head 4-bit RTN g64) = 11.85 GB, the ONLY published vLLM-loadable 27B that fits a 16 GB card -- every W4A16/AWQ/GPTQ build is 19.45-19.56 GB because it leaves the ~248k-vocab embedding at high precision. BOUND OPERATING POINT (operator decision D5 = A, 2026-09-16; its util 0.90 and 32 sequences SUPERSEDED 2026-09-30, and the util 0.87 / 8 sequences point that followed SUPERSEDED 2026-10-01, both by the co-residency re-measures at the end of this note): max_model_len 32,768 at util 0.90 -- KV 1.75 GiB = 43,690 tokens (1.33x), 13,852 MiB alone, and the mem0 embedder answers HTTP 200 beside it idle AND under 4-stream load (card peak 14,623 of 15,356 MiB); single-stream 7.17 tok/s, TTFT p50 1.66 s, 4-stream aggregate 20.36 tok/s (0 failed); blind quality at this window 8.42 (accuracy 9.54, zero fabrications; the llama.cpp IQ3_S+MTP arm 9.28). Why not the seat's own shape: alone it serves 49,152 at util 0.92 (KV 2.46 GiB = 65,967 tokens, 1.34x; 65,536 refused; blind 8.35; single-stream 5.75, 4-stream 19.53 tok/s) but holds 14,694 of 15,356 MiB, and the support group's embedder then returns HTTP 500 -- every mem0 write failed while the seat was warm; at util 0.90 vLLM refuses 49,152 (estimated maximum 32,928). The bound-lane fields are the config the digest-8 gate passed 8/8 at (3/8 at the 300 s wire default -- timeouts only, no wrong answers); agent_seat_tok_s 7.17 (the single-stream rate MEASURED at this operating point; 5.75 was the 49,152 @ 0.92 shape's) seeds the D-03 auto wall because no completion reaches the 1,024 tokens a rate sample needs. Cache server (as of 2026-09-16): BLOCKED, not chosen (D-117) -- LMCache 0.5.4's MP connector rejects vLLM 0.29's kv_layout. SUPERSEDED 2026-09-18 (register B-01): LMCache 0.5.5 carries the kv-layout fix, and the seat stays storeless for a VRAM reason instead, see storeless_reason. Records: 'Benchmarks and Optimizations/2026-09-16-16gb-tier-pass/' (judge-27b-49k, live-cutover/). CO-RESIDENCY RE-MEASURE 2026-09-30 (operator order: the memory embedder has absolute priority, so the seats make room for it and it is never the one excluded). On the ampere-16 reference box (NVIDIA A2, 15,356 MiB) with the embedder (embeddinggemma 300M Q8, 452 MiB) and the reranker (bge-reranker-v2-m3 Q4_K_M, 372 MiB) resident, the previous declaration (util 0.90, max_num_seqs 32) ran the engine at 14,788 MiB under four concurrent 8k-token requests -- about 1 GB over its util share, because graph capture and workspaces are sized for 32 sequences -- so the embedder could not load and every memory write failed for 35 minutes. Lowering util alone does not work: util 0.82 is refused (KV 0.64 GiB, but 1.29 GiB is needed for one 32,768-token request; vLLM's own estimate of the maximum length is 9,408) and util 0.87 with 32 sequences is refused (28 Mamba cache blocks for 32 sequences). DECLARED 2026-09-30 (SUPERSEDED 2026-10-01 by the next block): util 0.87 with max_num_seqs 8, window 32,768 unchanged -- KV pool about 34k tokens (about 1.0x the window, against the 1.33x above), engine peak 13,984 MiB under four concurrent 8,007-token requests, card peak 14,833 MiB with the embedder and the reranker resident (about 520 MiB of headroom), embedder answering in 25 ms. Cost: the seat serves at most 8 sequences at once, and its pool holds about one full window. Do not raise util or max_num_seqs without repeating this load beside both support models. CO-RESIDENCY RE-MEASURE 2026-10-01 (ADR 0049 Amendment 5, register A-122b; operator order: the memory stack's embedder AND reranker stay resident beside the seat with about 1 GiB free). On the ampere-16 reference box under a GPU lease, with four concurrent ~20k-token requests, a cold rerank 8 s into the load and rerank + embed every 2 s, the util 0.87 / max_num_seqs 8 / max_num_batched_tokens 4096 point above peaked at 14,717 MiB (seat 13,860 + embedder 460 + reranker 378, 639 MiB free; KV pool 50,176 tokens) and the reranker failed to start beside the loaded seat 7 times ('upstream command exited prematurely' in the node's llama-swap log). DECLARED NOW: util 0.84, max_num_seqs 4, max_num_batched_tokens 2048, window 32,768 and agent_ctx_tokens 32,768 unchanged, and the reranker served at --ctx-size 4096 --batch-size 2048 --ubatch-size 2048 (the memory stack's client scores each pair, truncated to 6,000 characters, as one non-causal sequence of at most about 2,000 tokens, which must fit one ubatch) -- KV pool 45,472 tokens (29 blocks of 1,568 = 1.39x the window), card peak 13,987 MiB (seat 13,204 + embedder 458 + reranker 306), 1,369 MiB free, and the four requests finished in 544 s where the util 0.87 point needed 900+ s. util 0.85 with 4 sequences did not start in that arm (unexplained, probably the previous engine still releasing VRAM; not re-run). The 35B seat kept util 0.85 / 8 / 4096 (969 MiB free beside the smaller reranker; superseded 2026-10-02 by util 0.855 on vLLM 0.30.0). Live on the reference box since 2026-10-01 19:31: seat warm in 52 s, /v1/rerank 3/3 with the seat loaded, idle 13,565 of 15,356 MiB. Do not raise util, max_num_seqs or max_num_batched_tokens without repeating this load beside both support models. vLLM 0.30.0 MOVE AND KV POOL PIN 2026-10-02 (registers A-119 and A-129; ADR 0049 Amendment 6). After the acceptance arms the ampere-16 reference box moved both vLLM seats to vLLM 0.30.0, so engine_min_version is 0.30.0. DECLARED NOW: the lane seat is started with --kv-cache-memory-bytes 1524713390 (kv_cache_memory_bytes), the 1.42 GiB pool vLLM 0.29.0 sized on a warm start (45,472 tokens, 1.39x the 32,768 window). vLLM ignores gpu_memory_utilization once kv_cache_memory_bytes is set (its CacheConfig documents the override), so util 0.84, max_num_seqs 4 and max_num_batched_tokens 2048 stay declared as the point the pool and the engine workspace were measured at, not as the pool size. WHY A PIN (register A-129): a utilization-sized pool is measured during startup profiling, device-wide, so a cold compile cache (profiled activation 0.77 GiB against 0.41 warm) or a memory-stack model loading in that window shrinks it below one 32,768-token request and the start fails ('To serve at least one request...'); reproduced on an empty card with the embedder fired at about 50 s, and three such production start failures were in this seat's log. MEASURED at vLLM 0.30.0 with the pin: card peak 13,951 of 15,356 MiB under four concurrent ~20k-token requests beside the embedder and the reranker (1,405 MiB free), digest-8 8/8 at the 900 s wall, and greedy output identical to 0.29.0 on 20 prompts. THERMAL CAVEAT (register A-130): sustained decode on the A2 throttles, so agent_seat_tok_s 7.17 and every other tok/s in this note are cool-card figures, not sustained ones. Do not change the pool, util, max_num_seqs or max_num_batched_tokens without repeating this load beside both support models.

Setting agent_thinking off (the policy it was measured under) did not help: 0/8. The 4B seat re-verified 8/8 at walls 36-132 s on the same set. So the QUALITY verdict stands unchanged (24/24 blind) and the seat is available by name for callers that pass timeout_sec up to the 900 s cap; it becomes the default binding when the wall is derived from the seat's measured rate (register D-03) rather than from a constant. AGENT SEAT RENDERED 2026-09-07 (0.113.33): this tier now declares a `vllm_seat` and the installer RENDERS it -- the systemd unit, the two llama-swap wrappers, the polkit rule and the llama-swap entry -- instead of pointing at a runbook. ADR 0035 originally recorded 'the tier SEED is unchanged: the seat is a hand-installed venv and unit, not something the installer renders', and the consequence was that every fresh ampere-16 install kept getting qwen3.5-4b-agent, the arm that LOST its own bake-off (8/8 at 159 s vs the vLLM seat's 8/8 at 45 s, 4x the window). Operator ruling 2026-09-07: install defaults follow the measurement, so render the seat. PREREQUISITES ARE NOT RENDERED and that is deliberate: the engine is a hand-built venv (vLLM 0.28, torch 2.13+cu130) plus an HF snapshot, so the installer DETECTS them and falls back to the llama.cpp seat with a stated reason when they are absent -- a unit pointing at a venv nobody built fails at boot, which is strictly worse than the fallback. THE RENDERED UNIT IS `vllm-agent-seat`, NOT the reference box's hand-installed `vllm-a2-seat`: a tier is a hardware class and must not name a unit after one machine's card. A box already running vllm-a2-seat keeps it -- running the installer there would create a SECOND unit on the same port, so stop and disable the old one first (`systemctl disable --now vllm-a2-seat`) or leave that box hand-managed. The deployment paths (stack/seat/venv dirs, HF home) are NOT tier fields either: they come from the install root and the box, because hardening one host's layout into a hardware tier is the mistake this table exists to avoid. SEAT JUSTIFICATION CORRECTED 2026-09-08 — THE EARLIER ONE WAS A SPEED ARGUMENT AND IS WITHDRAWN. The 2026-09-04 bake-off's score was `not deferred AND len(findings)>=3 AND len(summary)>40` -- a SHAPE check, which the harness's own acceptance linter classifies as SHAPE-ONLY ('passes garbage'). Both the 4B and the 12B cleared it 8/8, so 8/8 never meant 'equal quality', it meant 'both emitted well-formed output'; the seats were then separated on wall time, which is not a quality signal and is explicitly not how seats are chosen here. BLIND RE-EVALUATION 2026-09-08 on the RETAINED answers (they survived in the digest8-*.json records): the same 8 ADR-digest contracts, judged against the ground-truth ADRs by 3 independent lenses (faithfulness / substance / consumer-usefulness) = 24 judgements, candidates anonymised and order permuted per contract, with no model name, parameter count, engine or timing visible to any judge. Mean overall out of 10 -- qwen3.5-4b-vllm 7.58 (specificity 8.17, coverage 7.12, 0 filler findings, 12 of 24 firsts); qwen3.5-4b-agent llama.cpp 6.79 (7.29 / 6.21, 3 filler, 7 firsts); gemma4-12b-agent 6.38 (6.62 / 5.88, 1 filler, 5 firsts). All three lenses agreed on the ordering. So the vLLM seat IS the quality winner on this task shape and the binding stands -- but on quality evidence, not on 45 s vs 159 s. NUANCE THAT THE MEAN HIDES: the 12B fabricates least SEVERELY (its errors are vagueness and overstatement) while both 4Bs invent specifics, and the llama.cpp 4B inverted a NUMBER (asserting a '5-minute lease timeout' where the ADR says contract timeout + 5 minutes) -- the worst failure kind for a delegated digest. TWO THINGS THIS DOES NOT SHOW, both open: (1) it is ONE task shape, digesting an ADR into findings, and says nothing about longer reasoning, code or multilingual work; (2) THE 12B HAS NEVER RECEIVED THE vLLM TREATMENT. The engine alone moved the SAME 4B weights from 6.79 to 7.58 and removed every filler finding, which is a large effect, so a 12B served under vLLM (w4a16 or Q4, fp8_e5m2 KV) at a reduced window is the untested arm and is the next measurement this tier needs -- the llama.cpp 12B measured 7,512 MiB, so it plausibly fits at util ~0.85 with a 32-64k window. SUPERSEDED THE SAME DAY — THE 12B WAS RUN. gemma-4-12B-it-qat-w4a16-ct was already on the box (8.0 GB) and had been all along. Two spec defects had to be fixed to launch it (0.113.37): --limit-mm-per-prompt listed only image and video, so Gemma-4's audio tower was built anyway and vLLM died with AttributeError: 'Gemma4UnifiedAudioFeatureExtractor' object has no attribute 'fft_length'; and fp8_e5m2 KV is NOT free on Ampere but per-BACKEND (FlashAttention works for Qwen3.5, Triton refuses for Gemma-4 on the SAME card: 'native FP8 (fp8e4nv) requires SM89+'). It then needed util 0.95 to serve 32,768 (8.28 GiB weights, KV pool 48,925 tokens, 14,140 MiB) -- a 32k window where the 4B gets 131k on the same card. BLIND FOUR-WAY RESULT (same 8 contracts, same 3 lenses, 4 candidates per packet, Latin-squared, nothing about model/engine/timing visible to any judge), mean overall /10: qwen3.5-4b-vllm 7.75, qwen3.5-4b-agent 7.38, gemma4-12b-vllm 6.50, gemma4-12b-agent 6.21. The 2x2 separates the effects: ENGINE +0.38 on the 4B and +0.29 on the 12B; MODEL -1.17 on llama.cpp and -1.25 on vLLM. So the winning engine did NOT rescue the 12B -- it is worse by ~1.2 on BOTH engines and took 1 of 24 firsts, with all three lenses agreeing. The binding stands on QUALITY. What this still does not show: one task shape, and these are different model FAMILIES rather than sizes (Qwen3.5-4B vs Gemma-4-12B) -- Qwen3.5-9B-quantized.w4a16 is on the box if that is worth settling. The 12B does fabricate least severely (2 distinct vs 5-6), which matters where inventing beats omitting. Evidence: Benchmarks and Optimizations/2026-09-08-a2-seat-quality-reeval/. VISION SEAT MEASURED 2026-09-12 (0.116.1): qwen3-vl-8b (a J-media inheritance from blackwell-16, never run on this silicon) -> qwen38-27b-vision, Qwen3.8-27B UD-IQ3_S + mmproj-F16 at ctx 8192, reasoning off, 12.4 GiB resident. ampere-6.notes: Configs #10/#11 (3050 6GB). **MEASURED 2026-07-26** on an RTX 3050 6GB + i9-9900 + 32GB DDR4-2667 (spec: docs/specs/2026-07-26-ampere-6-tier-design.md). (1) RESIDENT TIER E2B -> E4B: E4B at 16K/q8_0 occupies only 3100 MiB of 6144, so the stronger workhorse fits with room to spare - a pure GPU-side win. (2) CTX 16K -> 32K: the projected 'may downshift to 8K' worry was unfounded; E4B reaches 64K/f16 in 4046 MiB and E2B 64K/f16 in 2078 MiB. 32K is chosen to leave GPU headroom for whatever else shares the card. (3) 'q8_0 KV is MANDATORY' was FALSE: Gemma-4 E-series uses a 512-token sliding window with only periodic global layers, so KV barely grows - f16 at 16K costs just 130 MiB more than q8_0. q8_0 is kept as the conservative default; f16 is available if a deployment wants it. (4) **26B STAYS DROPPED - THIS IS AN ARCHITECTURAL DECISION, NOT A CAPACITY LIMIT. DO NOT 'FIX' IT.** The 26B-A4B was measured to RUN here (--n-cpu-moe 24 serves at 32K, 210 pp / 13.5 tg), so a future reader WILL be tempted to enable it. Don't: any MoE tier puts experts in CPU+RAM, and boxes in this class are SERVERS whose CPU and RAM are reserved for their services - inference is confined to the GPU. Enabling it also pushes VRAM to ~5.3GB of 6144, starving a desktop session sharing the card. If a genuinely dedicated inference box ever lands in this profile, give it its OWN profile id rather than flipping this one. Throughput: E2B 2631 pp / 90.9 tg; E4B 1529 pp / 48.1 tg. The 70W power cap (not raisable) is the real limiter - the card sustains ~1639 MHz of a 2100 MHz max at 58W mean. NOTE for ZFS hosts: ARC grew to 19.9GB of 31GB here and is NOT counted in MemAvailable, so cap zfs_arc_max to keep the memory picture honest for the services. TIER-DOCTRINE PASS 2026-08-16: reviewed; seats are the best that fit — no change. **AGENT SEAT BOUND 2026-08-17 (qwen3.5-4b-agent) — the first measured sub-27B agent-seat decision the house has ever had.** 15 candidates across families were served on the reference RTX 3050 and scored on TWO task shapes with FABRICATION as the disqualifying axis: shape B (read 3 docs -> structured extraction, 18-fact gold set) and shape C (5-file fixture with distractors -> search+select, cross-file arithmetic with a unit conversion, conditional reasoning, and a fabrication trap). Qwen3.5-4B is the ONLY candidate strong on BOTH - 67% extraction (vs the e4b incumbent's 50%) and 4/5 search+reason - at 3681 MiB with ctx 32768 q8_0, which fits beside the resident support tier. Every other candidate fails one of the tier's FOUR mapped failure modes: (1) loop and never answer (qwen3.5-2b wins extraction at 78% then scores 1/5 on shape C, deriving right answers in prose and looping until the budget dies), (2) answer from partial reads (qwen3-30b-a3b scores the highest extraction of anything tested at 83% and then 1/5 - valid JSON with confidently WRONG content, which is worse for a delegation lane than returning nothing), (3) refuse tools entirely (ling-mini-2.0), (4) never emit valid JSON (lfm2.5). ZERO fabrications from any model across ~40 runs and both shapes - these models omit rather than invent, which is the property the delegation design depends on. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP matched the winner on both shapes and is REJECTED ON THIS TIER'S ROLE BOUNDARY, not on quality: it needs RSS 21.7 GB on a box whose baseline available RAM is 24.3 GB and which runs 24/7 services - recorded as the ceiling this tier could reach if a node were ever repurposed as a dedicated inference box. **TWO CONFIGURATION FACTS THAT ARE LOAD-BEARING, BOTH MEASURED - DO NOT 'TIDY' THEM AWAY.** (a) The seat's llama-swap entry writes its flags EXPLICITLY instead of using the ${common} macro, because ${common} pins `--reasoning off` and this is a THINKING model: measured at the deployed ctx, with a FRESH server per run (n=3 per arm, zero spread) the same seat scores 67%/67%/67% under llama.cpp's default reasoning and collapses to 28%/28%/28% with `--reasoning off`, while the search+reason shape is 4/5 on both arms — so reasoning-off costs half the extraction recall and buys nothing. The cascade's reasoning-off invariant must never be extended to this entry. (b) The AGENT PROFILE is the single biggest lever on this tier - same model, same contract, `--profile general` (the DEFAULT, 11 tools) scores 0% with zero output bytes while `--profile research` scores 72%. The delegation lane already defaulted to `research`, and this tier now SEEDS `agent_profile: research` so the other agent front doors (the `agent_run` MCP tool and the `local-agent` CLI) inherit it instead of falling to bare `general` by omission — that open question is CLOSED, on the measurement above. An explicit per-call/`--profile` value still wins, and `--two-tier` is exempt because it sets its own architect/editor toolsets. Full evidence: Benchmarks and Optimizations/2026-08-17-ampere6-seat-bakeoff/ (the tier matrix records the seat DECISION; benchmark data lives in the benchmarks folder, not in the workbook).

rockchip-rk3588.notes: Rockchip RK3588 SoC board (reference: <node-d>, RK3588S): 4x Cortex-A55 (cpu0-3) + 4x Cortex-A76 (cpu4-7), 7.7 GiB LPDDR4X shared by CPU, GPU and NPU (no dedicated VRAM), a 3-core 6 TOPS NPU and a Mali-G610 MP4 GPU. The board also runs the operator's home-automation stack, which decides the shape of the tier: NO model runs on the CPU (ADR 0054 amendment: no alt_backends, no CPU seat), uma_reserve_gib 3 holds RAM back for that stack (fleet-serve advertises MemTotal less the reserve as capacity and MemAvailable less it as free, about 4.7 GiB of inference budget), and every model unloads after five idle minutes (ttl 300). Detection reads the device tree's root compatible: `rockchip,rk3588` on the vendor 6.1 kernel (board token rockchip,rk3588s-exampleboard-5), `rockchip,rk3588s` on mainline 7.0 (board token vendor,exampleboard-5); both boot entries classify. NPU (the serving accelerator today): chat and vision run on the Rockchip RKLLM runtime through accelerators/rknpu/rkllm_server.py (rkllm seat qwen3.5-2b-npu, Qwen3.5-2B W8A8, a chat model and a VLM), and image classification, detection and embedding run on the rknpu accelerator sidecar (accelerators/rknpu/server.py). The NPU driver is built into the vendor kernel and is the out-of-tree rknpu 0.9.8 DKMS module on mainline; the in-tree rocket driver is a different stack that neither runtime uses. Qwen3.5-2B W8A8 is the largest RKLLM model that fits the budget (Qwen3.5-4B W8A8 is 5.58 GB, Gemma-4-E2B W8A8 7.98 GB; RK3588 has no W4 path). MEASURED 2026-09-30, mainline 7.0 + rknpu 0.9.8, RKLLM 1.3.1, one 1,256-token prompt: Qwen3.5-2B cpu_mask 0x0f (A55 x4) prefill 22.7 / decode 7.71 tok/s, 0xf0 (A76 x4) 126.4 / 7.14, VmHWM 2,260 MB at a 4096 window; Qwen3.5-0.8B 0x0f 44.5 / 9.07, 0xf0 174.5 / 16.67 (VmHWM 1,178 MB), and on the vendor 6.1 kernel with rknpu 0.9.7 the 0.8B read 0x0f 40.9 / 12.2, 0xe0 (A76 x3) 166.9 / 11.3, 0xf0 200.1 / 18.7, so mainline costs 10-15 % on this path. RKLLM refuses fewer enabled CPUs than the 3 NPU cores, so a cpu_mask needs at least three bits; the tier default is the A55 cluster 0x0f (strict CPU reservation for the host's own stack), which costs the 2B about 5x on prefill against the A76 cluster; the operator decides that trade. GPU, MEASURED 2026-09-30 and BLOCKED: the vendor kernel exposes the Mali as mali_kbase with an OpenCL blob only; mainline 7.0 uses panthor with Mesa 25.2.8 panvk (Vulkan 1.4, conformance 1.4.1.2, 'Mali-G610' as device 0, llvmpipe as device 1). llama.cpp b11270 built with GGML_VULKAN loads there, but its FIRST compute submission never finishes: panthor logs 'job timeout' and llama.cpp aborts with vk::DeviceLostError, on Qwen3.5-2B, Qwen3.5-4B and Gemma-4-E2B Q4 GGUFs alike, with flash-attn on or off and with batches down to 32 tokens on a freshly reset GPU. So this tier renders NO llama.cpp entry; its own template (llama-swap.linux-rk3588.yaml, not the stock vulkan one, which always renders offload-e4b at ~5 GB plus KV) keeps the Vulkan conventions for the day a Mesa/panthor/llama.cpp combination passes on this silicon. Re-measure before adding a GPU entry. vLLM has no Mali or RKNPU target, so this tier declares no vllm_seat. The media scripts this box cannot run (no ComfyUI, no sd.cpp, no TTS engine, no CPU inference) are seeded blank so the node does not advertise their lanes. VISION LANE (0.153.0): the NPU seat serves vqa and ocr only (media seat tasks, bound as vision_tasks): the runtime cannot constrain sampling and assess_image always sends a grammar, so the node refuses it at ack time, publishes vision_tasks in health, and a delegator places it elsewhere. The seat starts with repeat_penalty 1.1 because greedy decoding at 1.0 looped on VQA to the token cap (measured 2026-09-30, blind VQA 3/4 at 1.1). TEXT DOOR (0.154.0, DARK): the same runtime returns no logprobs either, so the tier binds unconstrained_seats (the seat model ids, written from the seat and never seeded) and the node's own pipeline runs classify and extract for this seat through a prompt that states the exact JSON shape plus a strict schema check (required keys, types, the label inside the allowed set, no extra key) instead of a grammar; a reply that fails is retried, then defers naming what failed. summarize and triage take the same validated path for a local call but are never admitted on the fleet. The seat declares NO text task, so the fleet text lane (POST /fleet/text, health text_tasks) is not advertised: blind check on this seat with no grammar, 2026-09-30, classify 4/4, extract 4/4, summarize 0/4, triage 0/4, and with no logprobs there is no uncertainty gate to catch a wrong answer. A later data-only change adds classify and extract to the seat tasks once at least 30 cases per lane run through the node pipeline score at least 90 percent correct with zero off-schema outputs accepted. Declaring a text task is meaningful only if this node cascade for that task (model, triage_model and any per-task rung) actually routes to the unconstrained seat, and the measurement must be taken through that same path. SERVING LIMITS seeded for the one-generation NPU: fleet_max_concurrent_jobs 1 (the NPU runs one generation at a time and the node default of 4 would queue three behind it, where their wait counts against a delegator's wall), request_timeout_sec 240 (below the delegator's 300 s fleet vision budget; the cold load measured 13 s), max_input_chars 8000 (about 2,000 tokens, which the A55 cluster prefills in about 90 s at the measured 22.7 tok/s), ocr_max_tokens 512 (at 7.71 tok/s decode the default 1024 would take over two minutes); fleet_max_queue_depth stays at its default, twice the concurrency (2: one running, one waiting), inside the NPU server's own window of one running and two waiting. NOT MEASURED: the 2B's resident size at its full 16384 window (the seat ships 8192 until it is) and at 8192, its answer quality against another tier's seat, the vision path's answers beyond the four-question check, and any agent seat (fleet_agent_enabled is false; none has been chosen).
